title: José López Portillo y Rojas to General Bernardo Reyes, 1909 (CEHM DLI.39.7680.2 and sibling records): a proposed numerical substitution key by Alberto Garvía García, partial and not yet verified

steps.what: The contributor aligned eight control sequences from two sibling telegrams of 15 and 23 July 1909 with their plaintexts: seven retained controls give 28 distinct number-to-letter values; an eighth, watermark-affected sequence (AYA) adds 60 = Y, provisional.
Project review of the count in issue #245: the strict count is 28; the images were not reachable from the project's environment, so nothing was compared with them.

Alberto Garvía García sent four CEHM viewer screenshots privately. An AI model read the seven control sequences and the 77 groups of the letter of 15 July on them: all numbers and plaintexts agree with the evidence file; the strict count stays 28, with no number mapped to two letters. With the same table the letter decodes to running Spanish (enemigo, te pronuncies, temor, calma y prudencia, oficios, clubs, Guadalajara) and the 29 July note to LIMANTOUR. Images are private and not in the repository (VERIFICATION.md).

Alberto Garvía García sent a second set of four clearer CEHM screenshots (1920 x 1080, from a computer), again private. An AI model re-read the controls, the letter and the 29 July note on them: all agree with the earlier check; the character after 77 is a typed s, not an e; the 29 July sequence reads 24 46 42 1 31 (CREEL); the group 28 23 24 54 2 is printed as given. The contributor reads that group as n-d-o-s-e (quejándose) with 24 as a slip for an o code, and compares the 48 in situación; the project records it as tentative, because it assumes one error (VERIFICATION.md section 5).

validation.notes: The statistical test needs the Spanish letter model (lang/, es-modern), whose corpus cannot be fetched from this environment (Gutenberg returns 403). The key was instead checked against seven control sequences with plaintext on the CEHM images and by the decoding of the letter into running Spanish (VERIFICATION.md); it is not independent of the reading.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Contributor's claim: ciphertext-only inference, then supported by the plaintexts of sibling telegrams. Not verified by the project.

outcome.notes: Key proposed by Alberto Garvía García (28 strict values, 60 = Y provisional), checked against the CEHM images by an AI reader on 6 Nov 2026 (VERIFICATION.md). Read in part: the letter of 15 July (segment C tentative) and the names in the note of 29 July.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Counted by hand from key.tsv and the decryption files: letter of 15 July 75 of 75 alphabetic groups read as letters of words (two of them, 24 in quejándose and 48 in situación, only by assuming a one-number slip; the codes 79 and 77 are not read) and the note of 29 July 9 of 14 (LIMANTOUR; the second name, 5 groups, is tentative and not counted): 84 of 89 = 94.4%. The control telegrams are not counted.

texts.label: López Portillo y Rojas to Bernardo Reyes, Mexico, 15 July 1909 (CEHM DLI.39.7680.2)
texts.summary: A friend of General Reyes, then governor of Nuevo León, warns him in July 1909 that the President speaks of him as an enemy and urges him not to declare himself at once, to keep calm and be prudent and to look after his health; other clubs of Guadalajara will write; he sends a pleading message the same day; the one complaint is quejándose (tentative).

reading_review.note: Read the decryption as Spanish sentences: enemigo, quejándose (24 as a slip for an o code, tentative), te pronuncies, temor, situación, calma, prudencia, oficios, clubs, Guadalajara form coherent clauses; two codes and one name are open.

texts.label: López Portillo y Rojas to Reyes, 29 July 1909: the cipher sequences (CEHM DLI.39.7712.1)
texts.summary: A short note of 29 July: there is a rupture between Limantour and (probably) Creel; the typed line asks Reyes to put his worries aside and read the reply carefully.

reading_review.note: Only two names are ciphered; LIMANTOUR is secure, the second name is tentative.

texts.label: The two control telegrams of 15 and 23 July 1909 (numbers and plain words)
texts.note: Cipher sequences beside their plaintext, used as the controls of the key; no running text. The images are private.
texts.summary: Short telegrams: the President is a declared enemy and postpones an explanation; Dr. Gómez must go; graves matters; clubs to be told to hold their replies.

prior.where: Two sibling telegrams of 15 and 23 July 1909 carry a contemporary plaintext (CEHM 118140, 118185), used by the contributor as controls. No prior reading of the letter found; issue #245, 4-6 Nov 2026.

human: Alberto Garvía García reported the key and the evidence (issue #245, pull request #308). The project has not seen the CEHM images and has verified none of the values.
